User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user in the GoalForge application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

coins.description: The number of coins the user has.

streak.description: The user's current streak of consecutive challenge completions.

goalId.description: Reference to the user's current Goal. (Relationship: User 1:1 Goal)

friendIds.description: References to the user's friends (other User ids). (Relationship: User N:N User)

id.description: Unique identifier for the goal entity.

description.description: A description of the goal (e.g., 'Lose 5kg', 'Learn Python').

startDate.description: The date and time when the goal was started.

userId.description: Reference to the user who set this goal. (Relationship: User 1:1 Goal)

ChallengeTemplate.title: ChallengeTemplate
ChallengeTemplate.description: Represents a template for a challenge, categorized by goal type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the challenge template.

goalType.description: The type of goal this challenge is associated with (e.g., 'Weight Loss', 'Coding').

description.description: The text description of the challenge (e.g., 'Drink 3L water', 'Solve 1 LeetCode problem').

UserChallenge.title: UserChallenge
UserChallenge.description: Represents a specific challenge assigned to a user for a particular day.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user challenge.

userId.description: Reference to the user who is assigned this challenge. (Relationship: User 1:N UserChallenge)

challengeTemplateId.description: Reference to the challenge template used to create this challenge. (Relationship: ChallengeTemplate 1:N UserChallenge)

assignedDate.description: The date when this challenge was assigned to the user.

completed.description: Indicates whether the user has completed the challenge.

completionTimestamp.description: The timestamp when the challenge was completed, or null if not completed.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure, scalable, and easily maintainable backend for the GoalForge application, adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). It uses denormalization to eliminate the need for `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations and simplifying debugging. The structure also segregates data based on access requirements to simplify security rules.

*   **User Data:** Stored under `/users/{userId}`. The structure utilizes path-based ownership, ensuring that only the authenticated user can access their own data.
*   **Goals:** Stored under `/users/{userId}/goals/{goalId}`. Goals are nested under the user, reinforcing ownership. This is a 1:N relationship between User and Goal.
*   **Challenge Templates:** Challenge templates are stored under `/challengeTemplates/{challengeTemplateId}` and are globally accessible, since they are templates, not user-specific instances.
*   **User Challenges:** User-specific challenges are stored under `/users/{userId}/userChallenges/{userChallengeId}`. This structure enables path-based ownership, allowing users to only access challenges assigned to them.

**Authorization Independence:** Achieved by denormalizing authorization data. For instance, if access to a goal needed to depend on user attributes, those attributes would be copied into the goal document. In this design, all subcollections are secured based on the parent user ID, enforcing strong ownership.

**QAPs Support:** The structure supports secure `list` operations by ensuring that each collection has a homogeneous security posture. For example, listing challenges under a user only returns challenges owned by that user, preventing unauthorized access to other users' data.
